newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen higher, pork bellies steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen higher, pork bellies steady to up.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.300 cent higher, analysts said.

Steady to higher cash hog indications on lighter hog marketings were expected to prompt carryover demand in hog futures. Packer interest for hogs is seen up following the fairly large advance in cutout values and easing hog marketings, analysts said.
Seasonal hog numbers will be declining soon going into the summer period, they said.
The market will also be keep an eye open for any news of stepped up exports to Japan, they added.

Pork belly futures were seen trading steady to higher on carryover support from Mondays sharp gains. The steady to firmer tone to cash bellies on reduced hog slaughter should keep futures supported, analysts said.
Expectations of a bullish Cold Storage report Friday should also offset any pressure from Tuesday's out-of-town report, they said.
Estimates on the out-of-town pork ranged from unchanged to in 500,000 lbs versus in 198,000 lbs last year.

Early analyst estimates on the Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouse as of May 31 ranged from 55.1 to 57 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 milloin lbs set in 1973.
